argument: Weak activity can set a temporary synaptic tag without producing durable memory, while strong activity triggers plasticity-related products. Tagged synapses can capture those products within a time window, converting transient changes into long-lasting potentiation and linking nearby events.
boundary: Molecular implementations and time windows differ across circuits and species.
Behavioral tagging may involve systems beyond local synapses.
The framework does not explain all forms of memory consolidation.
claim: Weak activity can set a temporary synaptic tag without producing durable memory, while strong activity triggers plasticity-related products. Tagged synapses can capture those products within a time window, converting transient changes into long-lasting potentiation and linking nearby events.
interpretation: This Principle gives a temporal-credit mechanism for consolidation, but child links should distinguish synaptic, cellular, and systems-level evidence.
